parents.subject: Food Science and Human Nutrition
parents.course: Advanced Topics in Food Science and Human Nutrition

ns2:section.sectionText: ***This is a two part class. You will be expected to take Nutritional Physiology 1 in Fall term for 1 credit hour and Nutritional Physiology II in Spring term for 2 credit hours.***Nutritional Physiology 1 will cover the following topics: Anatomy and physiology of the digestive, circulatory, integumentary, skeletal, and muscular system. The class will have a special focus on the absorption, distribution, storage, and mobilization of macronutrients and micronutrients; The student will learn the necessary concepts on cell biology and biochemistry required to understand human physiology; The manifestation of disease as a result of nutritional imbalances in body systems; Evaluation of the effectiveness and potential toxicity of nutritional supplements commonly used in the US; Pharmacological interventions and current therapeutics against diseases related to nutritional disorders. IMPORTANT: Nutritional Physiology I is the first part of a sequence, which will be completed in spring by taking Nutritional Physiology II.
